stem: The highest wheat-producing state of India is-
expl: India’s largest wheat-producing state is Uttar Pradesh. In 2024–25, Uttar Pradesh produced 35.65 million tonnes of wheat, which is the highest in India. After Uttar Pradesh, the second and third positions are respectively held by Madhya Pradesh (24.51 million tonnes) and Punjab (17.99 million tonnes). According to the Economic Survey 2025-26 wheat-producing states of India are—Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab.

stem: After Independence India progressed the maximum-

stem: Which fertilizer will you use for wheat cultivation?
expl: For wheat cultivation, nitrogenous fertilizer is used, which is available as urea.

stem: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
expl: In India, mainly three major crop seasons are considered-Kharif, Rabi and Zaid. Barley, gram and wheat- all three are Rabi crops. Sugarcane is technically an annual/long-duration cash crop. Compared to Rabi crops (barley, gram, wheat), sugarcane is placed more on the Kharif side because it requires higher temperature and relatively more water, and in the crop-classification of many states it is linked with the Kharif/monsoon-based season.

stem: Which of the following is the most important food crop in terms of cropped area?
expl: According to the Economic Survey, 2025-26, in 2024-25 rice was sown on 51.3 million hectares in India, while wheat was sown on 32.8 million hectares. Thus, in terms of cultivated area, rice is the most important food crop in India.

stem: In 2020, which of the following crops had the highest acreage in India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: In 2020, and even at present, rice has the largest area among the crops grown in India. In 2024-25, the top three rice-producing states in India were Uttar Pradesh, Telangana and West Bengal. As per 2023 data, at the global level, China ranks second after India in rice production.

stem: The region known as the Rice Bowl of India is –
expl: As per the given options, the Krishna-Godavari Delta region is called the “Rice Bowl” of India. This region falls in Andhra Pradesh. According to 2024-25 data, rice is produced in Andhra Pradesh on 2.08 million hectares of the total cultivated area. Here, the major rice-producing belt is spread across the Krishna-Godavari Delta regions. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

stem: Which is the most suitable crop for dryland farming?
expl: Among the given options, groundnut is the most suitable crop for dry land. It is a rain-fed Kharif crop. Wheat is mainly a temperate Rabi crop, which is grown in areas having irrigation facilities. Sugarcane is a tropical crop, and its cultivation is mostly carried out in irrigated areas or in humid and sub-humid climatic regions.

stem: Which one of the following coffee-growing areas is not in Karnataka?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Coffee Board of India, Coffee production is famous in Chikmagalur, Kodagu (Coorg) and Hassan districts of Karnataka; Wayanad, Travancore and the Nelliampathy region of Kerala; and Pulney Hills, Nilgiri, Shevaroy (Salem) and Annamalai (Coimbatore) regions of Tamil Nadu. Baba Budangiri is located in Karnataka, where coffee was first introduced in India.

stem: Which one of the following hills do not have tea plantations?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the given options, there are no tea gardens on Girnar hill. Tea gardens are found on all the other hills. Kannan Devan Hills are located in the Idukki district of Kerala, near the Munnar hill station. Tea plantations in the Munnar region began in the 1870s. Nilgiri is an important mountain region of the Western Ghats in southern India. Darjeeling is mainly famous for tea production and is located in West Bengal. Girnar Mountain is located in Gujarat, where tea plantations have not developed. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).
